land.text: the state north of the Po that Napoleon set up after Lodi (May 1796), enlarged on 19 May 1797 with the territories of the former Duchy of Modena

predecessors.note: Transpadane Republic has no Cliopatria row and no dossier yet (see notes).

land.text: 'The rest of Cispadania was merged into the Cisalpine Republic on 27 July' 1797

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's row 'Cispadane Republic' is dated 1800-1802 and is a different thing (see notes).

land.text: the whole republic, renamed on 26 January 1802

successors.note: 'In January 1802, the Consulta decided to change the name of the State to the Italian Republic'; infobox 'Renamed Italian Republic: 26 January 1802'. The Wikipedia page treats this as one state; the project keeps two dossiers because Cliopatria has two rows.

capitals.name: Milan
capitals.note: Infobox 'the capital of the unified state being Milan'.

keyframe_review.note: 41,872 km2 for 1797-1798 against the infobox 'Area (1797): 42,500 km2' (ratio 0.99). The shape covers Lombardy, Emilia, the Romagna, Mantua, the Valtellina (Sondrio), and also Verona, Rovigo (Venetian terraferma) and northern Marche cells (Pesaro e Urbino, 5 cells) that no opened page assigns to the republic; the page dates the Mincio (Mantua) department only to 26 May 1798 and the Rubicone (Forli) department to the constitution of 31 August 1798, so Cliopatria draws them a year early; kept, the ledger gives the page's dates.

42,059 km2, the same extent; the year is the Austro-Russian conquest ('Occupied by Austria: 27 April 1799'), so from 27 April the land is occupied, not Cisalpine; the ledger carries the loss and the restoration. Novara (annexed 13 October 1800) is not yet in.

correction.text: the restored republic: the 1799 extent, with Novara annexed on 13 October 1800, to the Adige frontier of 9 February 1801

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1800-1802: Cliopatria has no Cisalpine shape after 1799 (its 'Cispadane Republic' row 1800-1802, 7,095 km2, is far too small for a republic of 42,500 km2). 'Restored by France: 2 June 1800'; the shape is the 1799 one with Novara added on 13 October 1800 (ledger) and the Adige frontier of the Treaty of Luneville (9 February 1801).

region.text: the Romagna region ceded under the Treaty of Tolentino

ledger.note: 1797: the Romagna passes from the Pope. 'Under the Treaty of Tolentino, Pope Pius VI was forced to cede the Romagna region'; neither opened page dates the treaty, and the Cisalpine page names the Rubicone (Forli) department only in the reorganisation of 31 August 1798. Cliopatria draws the Romagna inside from 1797.

region.text: the Transpadane Republic with the former Duchy of Modena, the republic of 29 June 1797

ledger.note: 29 June 1797: Napoleon decrees the Cisalpine Republic at Milan. 'on 12 Messidor (29 June), he decreed the birth of the Cisalpine Republic'; infobox 'Established: 29 June 1797', 'Constitution adopted: 8 July 1797'; on 19 May 1797 he had 'transferred the territories of the former Duchy of Modena to Transpadania'. Eleven departments in 1797.

region.text: the territories of the former Duchy of Modena (the Panaro and Crostolo departments)

ledger.note: 19 May 1797 (before the decree): Modena passes to Transpadania. 'On 19 May 1797, Napoleon transferred the territories of the former Duchy of Modena to Transpadania'; the Panaro (Modena) and Crostolo (Reggio) departments are among the 1797 eleven.

region.text: the rest of Cispadania, merged on 27 July

ledger.note: 27 July 1797: the Cispadane Republic joins the Cisalpine. 'The rest of Cispadania was merged into the Cisalpine Republic on 27 July.' The page lists Bologna (Reno) and Ferrara (Basso Po) only in the 1798 departments, so the Bologna and Ferrara part is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Valtellina, seceded from the Three Leagues

ledger.note: 22 October 1797: the Valtellina joins the Republic. 'On 1 Brumaire (22 October), Bonaparte announced the union of Valtelline with the Republic', after its secession from the Swiss Three Grey Leagues; the same page says the republic took 'Valtellina and Campione d'Italia'. Sondrio province is the researcher's reading of the Valtellina.

26 May 1798: the Mincio department (Mantua) is added. 'Mincio (Mantua) on 7 Prairial (26 May)' 1798. The page does not say who held Mantua before; the Habsburg monarchy is the neighbour on the east in Cliopatria's seed.

region.text: the whole republic, occupied by Suvorov's Russian and Austrian forces

ledger.note: 27 April 1799: the Austro-Russian army takes the republic after Cassano. Infobox 'Occupied by Austria: 27 April 1799'; 'After the defeat of France at the Battle of Cassano in April 1799'; they 'departed only on 30 May 1800'. An occupation, not an annexation: the republic is restored in 1800. [Reviewer eu-20-a, 2026-10-31: type loss -> occupation_start: the infobox reads 'Occupied by Austria: 27 April 1799' and habsburg-monarchy records the same occupation (L112, occupation_start cisalpine-republic, 1799-04).]

region.text: the whole republic, restored after the Austro-Russian occupation

ledger.note: June 1800: France restores the republic. Infobox 'Restored by France: 2 June 1800' (the text says 15 Prairial year VIII, 4 June 1800); 'They departed only on 30 May 1800'. [Reviewer eu-20-a, 2026-10-31: type gain -> occupation_end: 'Restored by France: 2 June 1800'; habsburg-monarchy L114 ends its occupation in 1800-05.]

region.text: Novara, the border moved from the Ticino to the Sesia

ledger.note: 13 October 1800: Novara is annexed. On 21 Vendemiaire (13 October 1800) Napoleon 'ordered the annexation of Novara to the republic', which moved the western border 'from the river Ticino to the River Sesia', after the king 'refused to sign a treaty of peace' over occupied Piedmont.

region.text: the whole republic under its new name

ledger.note: 26 January 1802: the Cisalpine Republic becomes the Italian Republic. Infobox 'Renamed Italian Republic: 26 January 1802'; 'the Consulta decided to change the name of the State to the Italian Republic'; Bonaparte is its president.

wars.name: Italian campaign of 1796-1797 (War of the First Coalition)

zones.text: Lombardy north of the Po, after Lodi (10 May 1796)

wars.outcome: Beaulieu's Austrians lost Lodi on 10 May 1796; Sardinia accepted the Armistice of Cherasco on 28 April; Austria asked for the Peace of Leoben (18 April 1797) and signed Campo Formio on 17 October 1797, acknowledging the Cisalpine Republic.
wars.note: The Cisalpine page: 'After the Battle of Lodi (May 1796), Napoleon set up two states, one on each side of the Po'.

wars.name: Austro-Russian conquest of northern Italy

zones.text: the republic occupied from 27 April 1799 to 30 May 1800

wars.outcome: After Cassano the Cisalpine Republic was occupied by Suvorov's forces; Napoleon restored it in June 1800 and the Treaty of Luneville (9 February 1801) set the frontier with the Holy Roman Empire 'on the River Adige'.

certainty.note: Departmental lists with dates (eleven departments in 1797, Mincio 1798, Novara 1800) and the Adige frontier of 9 February 1801. The frontier with Austria before the Treaty of Campo Formio (17 October 1797) and the Papal and Piedmontese lines in 1797-1799 are provisional and soft.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Cisalpine Republic' 1797..1799 (two shapes of 41,872 and 42,059 km2, infobox 42,500). The state continues to 26 January 1802 on the page and the 'italian-republic' dossier (another part) starts on that day with this one as predecessor, so this dossier runs to 1802 and adds a new keyframe for 1800-1802, which Cliopatria lacks. Cliopatria's 'Cispadane Republic' row (1800-1802, 7,095 km2) does not describe the 1796-1797 Cispadane Republic and lies inside the years of the restored Cisalpine; the cispadane-republic dossier should say what it is. Needs a dossier: 'Transpadane Republic' (1796-1797, set up after Lodi; no Cliopatria row), 'Three Leagues' (the Grisons, Valtellina's lord until 1797), and the former Duchy of Modena before 1815 (the duchy-of-modena-and-reggio row begins 1815). Dates the opened pages do not give: Treaty of Tolentino (the Romagna cession is recorded at year 1797, confidence 1), the Bologna and Ferrara legations (listed only in the 1798 departments), the fall of Mantua, Bergamo and Brescia leaving Venice, the Republic of Crema, the 1801 Adige line beyond the Treaty of Luneville date. The Cisalpine page's infobox lists Venice and the Republic of Crema as predecessors without saying what land. The 1798 French alliance (signed 8 June 1798) and the second constitution (31 August 1798) are not territorial; the client relation to France is recorded as vassal_start in french-directory. Gazetteer: no new names needed ('Reggio Emilia', 'Sondrio', 'Mantova', 'Novara' resolve).
